transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2027-02-14 15:00 PT
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SA), Evan Morris (Hawthorn CISO), Priya Desai (Head of Cloud Eng), Aisha Khan (Security Engineer), Tom Alvarez (Procurement)

Summary (auto): Quick intro then deep dive on compliance posture. Customer wants clear answers on SOC2/ISO evidence, KMS control, SSO/SAML, RBAC and audit logs before procurement greenlight.

00:00 Jordan Hayes: Hey everyone thanks for taking the time, I'm Jordan with Redwood. Maya and Luis are with me, they run our security and infra side. How's everybody doing?
00:08 Evan Morris: Doing well, thanks. We said 30-40 min so we'll be concise. We're trying to validate whether Redwood's Hosted product meets our security bar or if we need Dedicated/Private deployment.
00:20 Jordan Hayes: Perfect, that's what we'd like to cover - SOC 2/ISO, IdP integration, key management, auditability, retention. Maya you want to kick off on the technical controls?
00:28 Maya Chen: Sure. Quick note, transcription may garble some acronyms - I'll say K V cache sometimes, but K V cache not critical here, apologies. So broadly Redwood supports hosted with customer data logically separated, Dedicated where you reserve GPU pools, and a Private deployment that runs in your VPC. For keys we integrate with customer KMS, you can bring your own keys or use customer-managed crypto in Dedicated/Private.
00:55 Priya Desai: On the KMS point - we run keys in AWS KMS with multi-region CMKs and strict key rotation. For Hosted, will Redwood be able to use our CMKs in our account or do we have to hand keys over?
01:10 Maya Chen: For Hosted we typically use service-managed keys, but we offer a Bring-Your-Own-Key flow for enterprise customers for encryption at rest via a cross-account grant for AWS KMS or via external HSM in Private. For Dedicated we can either bring keys into the Dedicated environment or configure cross-account CMK grants. We'll include the technical design doc.
01:30 Evan Morris: Okay, that helps. Also SOC 2 - do you have a Type II? And ISO 27001? We need evidence for procurement.
01:38 Jordan Hayes: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications; we'll send the reports and SSP. I can put the link in the follow-up email.
01:47 Tom Alvarez: From procurement we'll want a redacted SOC2 and the auditor name and the coverage dates.
01:52 Jordan Hayes: Absolutely. We'll send the redacted reports, auditor firm and scope.
01:58 02:00 Maya Chen: On SSO - Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and OIDC, and SCIM for provisioning. We've seen IdPs like Okta, Azure AD, Ping. You can do SP-initiated or IdP. For RBAC we have roles aligned to least privilege - org admin, billing, app-deployer, viewer, and token scoping so API keys can be scoped to routes and models.
02:22 Aisha Khan: Do API tokens show owner and usage in audit logs? We need immutable audit trails for access and model prompts for any PII handling.
02:30 Luis Ortega: Yes, audit logs include token id, user (SSO identity or service-account), route called, model used, latency/cost metrics; we also retain request/response headers and can support exporting logs to your SIEM via S3 or push to your logging endpoint. There may be redaction options for prompt content depending on policy.
02:48 Evan Morris: How long do you retain logs by default and is retention configurable? Our policy is 7 years for certain transactional logs, but for prompts we want shorter.
02:58 Maya Chen: Default retention is 90 days in Hosted analytics, but for Dedicated/Private you get full control and can ship logs to your retention platform or configure longer retention in the cluster. We can set up S3 export with lifecycle policies to meet 7-year cold storage. For prompts specifically, we recommend configured redaction and configurable retention per log type.
03:20 Priya Desai: Data residency - we operate EU + US regions. For Hosted do you guarantee region isolation for model processing?
03:28 Jordan Hayes: We have multi-region hosting and routing policies. You can pin requests to region, and for enterprise we can ensure processing in a selected region. For strict legal needs Private deployment in your VPC may be required.
03:38 Aisha Khan: On encryption in transit - do you use mTLS between components? What's the chain for inter-node traffic?
03:44 Luis Ortega: We use TLS 1.3 internally, mTLS for Dedicated/Private clusters with customer-provided certs. In Hosted, inter-service traffic is in our VPC with TLS and internal PKI; we can present network diagrams.
03:55 Tom Alvarez: Are there any third-party subprocessors we should be aware of?
04:00 Jordan Hayes: We list subprocessors in our data processing addendum. Primary ones are cloud providers for infrastructure, monitoring/logging providers for Hosted telemetry, and our CDN for console assets. We can provide a current subprocessor list and agreements.
04:12 Evan Morris: For regulatory audits, will Redwood allow auditor assessments or read-only access to logs?
04:18 Jordan Hayes: We support auditor questionnaires, we provide evidence packs, and for Dedicated/Private customers we can arrange more direct evidence or a co-located audit on request. We'll surface exactly what's possible in the SOC2/ISO pack.
04:30 04:40 Maya Chen: Quick note about model fallbacks - there are policy controls for routing, but from a security perspective you can restrict model variants and pin to versions so that evals are deterministic. Also, we'll preserve KV cache security with encryption at rest.
04:55 Priya Desai: Regarding RBAC - can we enforce least privilege for internal teams and have scoped service tokens for our app? We don't want blanket admin keys floating around.
05:04 Luis Ortega: Yes, tokens are scoped. You can tie tokens to service accounts provisioned via SCIM. Also support for temporary tokens and rotation via our API.
05:14 Aisha Khan: How about secrets management - are tokens stored encrypted and can you integrate with our HashiCorp Vault?
05:20 Maya Chen: Yes, we can integrate with Vault in Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports token rotation and encrypted storage, and we have a Vault integration option for enterprise.
05:30 Evan Morris: Any SOC 2 exceptions or open issues in last audit we should be aware of?
05:35 Jordan Hayes: Nothing material; we'll provide a summary of open remediation items from last audit.
05:40 Tom Alvarez: On procurement timing - if the security answers are clean we could move to legal and then pilot. Pricing wise, we want options for a short Dedicated pilot vs hosted credits.
05:51 Jordan Hayes: We can structure a pilot: 3-4 week benchmark on Dedicated with a scoped commit or Hosted pilot with stricter data controls; Maya can propose the runbook.
06:02 Maya Chen: For the deep dive, I'll want Aisha and Priya's infra folks on the call. We'll bring a runbook: networking, KMS config, SSO metadata, sample audit log export, and a lightweight perf benchmark for latency and token cost.
06:18 Aisha Khan: Sounds good. We'll need an architecture diagram for the Private deployment option showing VPC peering, ENIs, and KMS flow.
06:26 Luis Ortega: We'll provide that. Also note Dedicated uses isolated GPU pools and we can pin models to dedicated instances to control noise from multi-tenancy.
06:36 Evan Morris: Are there encryption-at-rest proofs? Will Redwood provide proof materials for disk encryption on nodes?
06:42 Jordan Hayes: Yes, we provide documentation of disk encryption, KMS use, and HSM options for Private. We'll include kernel cipher details in the compliance packet.
06:52 Priya Desai: Any limitations on bringing our own model or artifact storage? We may want to host model artifacts in our S3 and have Redwood pull them.
07:02 Maya Chen: For Private and Dedicated we support pulling artifacts from your S3 with IRSA roles; Hosted has a curated model catalog but we can talk about private model hosting as a managed feature for enterprise.
07:16 Evan Morris: If we go Hosted, how do you handle prompt data retention and PII? We need to ensure PII is not stored longer than policy and that we can request deletion.
07:26 Jordan Hayes: We have retention controls and can configure prompt retention to be minimal; Hosted has a default short retention but for strict PII requirements Dedicated or Private is recommended. We also support deletion APIs and data subject request workflows.
07:40 Aisha Khan: Audit logs - we want immutable logs with cryptographic hashing for tamper evidence, is that supported?
07:48 Luis Ortega: We can support append-only logs and S3 object versioning, and we can provide log exports with checksums. For cryptographic ledgering we can integrate with your existing ledger or provide signed log digests. We'll capture the specific requirement and propose options.
08:06 Tom Alvarez: Legal will want DPIA info and a data processing addendum.
08:11 Jordan Hayes: We'll include the DPA and privacy docs in the follow-up.
08:16 08:20 Evan Morris: One more - what's the incident response SLAs and communication channels? For example, if there's a data incident, how quickly do you notify and do you provide forensics artifacts?
08:29 Jordan Hayes: We have an incident response playbook; notification windows depend on severity but we commit to notification within 72 hours for major incidents and provide forensic artifacts where available. For enterprise customers we can arrange faster channels and dedicated incident liaisons.
08:46 Priya Desai: From a network perspective, do you support VPC peering vs private link? We prefer private link for minimal exposure.
08:53 Luis Ortega: We support private link for cloud integrations and VPC peering for Private deployments. We'll show pros/cons.
09:02 Aisha Khan: Can you give an example of the audit log schema? We need fields like timestamp, token_id, user_id, action, model, request_hash.
09:12 Maya Chen: Yes, sample schema will be shared. It includes request_id, timestamp, user_identity, token_id, route, model, request_size, response_size, latency_ms, and optional hashed prompt content. We'll share a CSV/JSON sample.
09:26 Evan Morris: Great. On the SSO side, do you support SCIM group sync to map groups to RBAC roles?
09:32 Jordan Hayes: Yes, SCIM group sync is supported. You can map groups to roles and have provisioning managed.
09:38 Tom Alvarez: Anything else on compliance for procurement? We need indemnities and SOC 2 evidence.
09:44 Jordan Hayes: We'll surface standard contract terms; legal can provide redlines later.
09:48 09:50 Maya Chen: Quick plug for the benchmark - we'll run a small perf test that highlights latency percentiles and token cost across model variants; this will help you weigh cost vs latency tradeoffs for Hosted vs Dedicated.
10:04 Priya Desai: That would be useful. Also please include quantization options and how they affect latency/cost.
10:11 Maya Chen: Will do; quantization profiles and expected perf deltas will be part of the runbook.
10:18 Evan Morris: Okay, this is very helpful. I think next steps are receipt of the SOC/ISO artifacts, the security pack, and scheduling the deep dive.
10:28 Jordan Hayes: Correct. We'll follow up with the artifacts and propose times for the deep dive (Maya + Luis).
10:33 Tom Alvarez: From procurement I'd like cost options laid out: Hosted metered, Dedicated pilot price, and Private setup estimate.
10:40 Jordan Hayes: We'll include sample pricing scenarios in the follow-up.
10:45 10:50 Maya Chen: Anything else from the Hawthorn side?
10:52 Aisha Khan: I'll gather KMS details and SSO metadata and send ahead of the deep dive.
10:58 Priya Desai: I'll get our infra folks available for the technical deep dive.
11:03 Evan Morris: Good. Thanks everyone.
11:06 Jordan Hayes: Thanks all - recap in our last 2 minutes: Jordan to send SOC2/ISO redacted reports + compliance pack; Maya to send runbook + schedule deep dive; Luis to prepare Private/Dedicated architecture diagram; Hawthorn (Aisha/Priya) to share KMS and IdP metadata. We'll target the deep dive next week.
11:28 End of call

Notes: There are some small transcription errors (K V cache etc) - quality medium. Shared artifacts referenced: "SOC2_redacted_v2.pdf", "Redwood_Security_Pack_link", "Dedicated_deepdive_runbook_v1.pdf", "audit_log_schema_sample.json".
